title: NFL Logo Quiz: Hard Mode
headline: Can You Name The NFL Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Logo?
description: A hard NFL logo quiz: eight tiny pieces of NFL team logos, about 2% of each logo. Guess the team, tap to reveal the answer, keep score and share your result.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current NFL team logo, about one fiftieth of the whole mark. No helmets, no wordmarks, no giveaways. Each piece still has one real detail in it, a color pair, a curve or an edge that belongs to only one team.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.piece: The red stripe running through the falcon's black wing.
items.fact: The Falcons' current logo arrived in 2003, and the bird is drawn so its body and wings form a capital F.

items.piece: A silver fang and the blue outline of the panther's open jaw.
items.fact: Carolina sharpened the panther in 2012, giving it a more muscular face and a more aggressive snarl.

items.piece: The gold and green rim at the top right of the oval.
items.fact: The G oval first went on Packers helmets in 1961, which makes it one of the oldest logos in the league.

items.piece: A front leg of the charging buffalo, under its chest.
items.fact: The charging buffalo has been the Bills' logo since 1974. Before that, the helmet carried a standing red buffalo.

items.piece: The orange rays of the sunburst, with the tip of the aqua dolphin.
items.fact: Miami's 2013 redesign took the helmet off the dolphin, which had worn one in every version since 1966.

items.piece: The red edge at the bottom of the bull's face.
items.fact: The Texans' bull head has been their logo since their first season in 2002, with the white star standing in for the Lone Star State.

items.piece: The bottom curve of the red C in KC.
items.fact: Founder Lamar Hunt is credited with sketching the arrowhead himself, borrowing the idea from the 49ers' interlocking SF.

items.piece: The very tip of the cardinal's crest.
items.fact: The Cardinals redrew the bird in 2005 with a sharper crest and a meaner eye, the version still in use.
